questions.questionHtml:
Two more exotic relational algebra operators are the semijoin (⋉)(⋉) and antijoin (▹)(▹). Semijoin is the same as natural join, except only attributes of the first relation are returned in the result. For example, if we have relations Student(ID, name)Student(ID, name) and Enrolled(ID, course),Enrolled(ID, course), and not all students are enrolled in courses, then the query "Student ⋉⋉ Enrolled" returns the ID and name of all students who are enrolled in at least one course. In the general case, E1⋉E2E1⋉E2 returns all tuples in the result of expression E1E1 such that there is at least one tuple in the result of E2E2 with matching values for the shared attributes. antijoin is the converse: E1▹E2E1▹E2 returns all tuples in the result of expression E1E1 such that there are no tuples in the result of E2E2 with matching values for the shared attributes. For example, the query "Student ▹▹ Enrolled" returns the ID and name of all students who are not enrolled in any courses.

🔥 GATE 2027 Original: Computer Networks - Transport Layer

A sender and receiver are connected by a 1 Gbps ($10^9$ bps) point-to-point link with a one-way propagation delay of 10 ms. The Maximum Segment Size (MSS) is 1 KB ($1000$ bytes). To achieve 100% link utilization with a sliding window protocol without delayed ACKs, what is the minimum number of bits required for the sequence number field in the packet header?

💡 Detailed Concept & Solution:
Bandwidth $B = 10^9$ bps.
Round Trip Time $RTT = 2 \times 10\text{ ms} = 20\text{ ms} = 0.02$ s.
Bandwidth-Delay Product $BDP = B \times RTT = 10^9 \times 0.02 = 2 \times 10^7$ bits $= 2.5 \times 10^6$ bytes.
Packet size $L = 1000$ bytes.
Optimal window size in packets $W = \frac{2.5 \times 10^6}{1000} = 2500$ packets.
For Selective Repeat (or general sliding window where max window is $W$), sequence number space must satisfy $N \ge 2W = 2 \times 2500 = 5000$.
Number of bits $= \lceil \log_2(5000) \rceil = 13$ (or if Go-Back-N, $N \ge W + 1 = 2501 \implies \lceil \log_2(2501) \rceil = 12$ bits).

Consider a computer design in which multiple processors, each with a private cache memory, share global memory using a single bus. This bus is the critical system resource.

Each processor can execute one instruction every 500500 nanoseconds as long as memory references are satisfied by its local cache. When a cache miss occurs, the processor is delayed for an additional 2,0002,000 nanoseconds. During half of this additional delay, the bus is dedicated to serving the cache miss. During the other half, the processor cannot continue, but the bus is free to service requests from other processors. On average, each instruction requires 22 memory references. On average, cache misses occur on 11 percent of references.

What proportion of the capacity of the bus would a single processor consume, ignoring delays due to competition from other processors?
